- When sentiment turns negative or shows strong bearish momentum (e.g., -1.00 or multiple 0.00s), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is consistently bullish (e.g., 1.00s across 5+ days), model may overfit upward trend; apply downward bias of 1–3% if price drops below 3-day SMA.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; use 14-day EWMA or 7-day rolling mean to anchor forecast.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in sentiment shift (e.g., if sentiment drops day 4, forecast should drop by day 6).
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals without sentiment confirmation; if sentiment remains flat or negative for 3+ days, model should not project >1% upward movement.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; cap forecast at 10–15% below 30-day moving average if sentiment is bearish or neutral.
